clue.text: For no reward, he drew young children

definitions.text: For no reward, he drew young children

parts.words: For no reward, he drew young children
parts.note: the legendary Hamelin piper, cheated of his fee for clearing the rats, piped the town's children away; 'drew' sounds like sketching

explanation.surface: An artist sketches children without being paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drew' looks like drawing pictures, but here it means led or lured away: the piper of Hamelin, refused his payment, drew the children out of town.
explanation.definitionFit: In the folk tale the unpaid piper of Hamelin led the town's children off.

clue.text: Father taking short knife to eat this?

definitions.text: Father taking short knife to eat this?

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: short means the word is cut off before its last letter

parts.note: to knife someone is to stab them

explanation.surface: Dad picks up a little knife to tuck into his dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims STAB to STA. The whole clue doubles as the definition: something you might eat with a knife (and fork).
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti, penne and other Italian noodle dishes are what a diner might attack with cutlery.

clue.text: Rival political project in Europe held up

parts.note: EMU is European Monetary Union, the single-currency scheme
delayed, so late

explanation.surface: A competing European political scheme has been delayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rival' looks like an adjective or noun but is the verb: to rival is to match or copy.
explanation.definitionFit: To rival someone is to equal or imitate their achievement, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Forced to admit performance was rehearsed

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: prised (open) means forced
an act is a performance

explanation.surface: Someone was made to confess that the show had been practised beforehand.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rehearsed has been gone over beforehand, made skilled by repetition.

clue.text: Decrepit man collapsed in corner

indicators.note: a collapsed structure has its parts thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A frail old man fell down in the corner of the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corner' is not a place but a plight, as in being in a tight corner.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a corner means being in an awkward, difficult situation.

clue.text: Hard liquor Burns's body came through

definitions.meaning: a strong grain whiskey, as in American or Canadian spirits
Robert Burns's song runs 'Gin a body meet a body comin' thro' the' grain field

explanation.surface: A strong drink once passed through the poet Burns's body.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Burns was Scotland's national poet; his song 'Comin' Thro' the Rye' has a body coming through a field of this grain.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirit distilled from this cereal is a kind of whiskey; the cereal field is where Burns's body walked.

clue.text: Carpeting is freely available?

parts.note: something on tap is freely available

explanation.surface: Floor covering is being offered at no cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tapis' is the old word for a tablecloth or carpet, kept in the phrase 'on the tapis', under discussion.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapis is a tapestry or floor covering, so it is carpeting.

clue.text: Timber initially one used for fencing temporary shelter

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word that precedes it

parts.note: an epee is a sword used in the sport of fencing

explanation.surface: Wood is the first thing used to put up a fence around a makeshift shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fencing' looks like putting up fences, but it is the sword sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A tepee is a conical tent of skins or canvas, a portable dwelling.

clue.text: One for whom Shaw wrote play with words about girl

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a pun is wordplay
Rita is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A play by Shaw is described as playing with words concerning a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: George Bernard Shaw published 'Three Plays for Puritans' (1901). 'play' looks like Shaw's drama but is part of 'play with words'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaw's collection 'Three Plays for Puritans' names this strict moralist as its intended reader.

clue.text: Say, Medea, Alcestis, or Ceres stage parts

indicators.note: parts suggests a piece taken from within the words that follow, running across them

explanation.surface: Medea, Alcestis or Ceres are roles that actresses play on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' looks like stage roles but signals that the answer is found inside 'alcestiS OR CERES Stage'. Medea, in Greek myth, was a witch.
explanation.definitionFit: Medea, the Colchian princess of Greek myth, was a witch skilled in magic, an example of the type.

clue.text: Mince us a herb, for flavouring this sort of roll?

indicators.note: to mince is to chop up, so these letters are cut and rearranged

parts.note: sage is a culinary herb

explanation.surface: A recipe: chop us a herb to season this kind of roll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mince' turns US A into SAU. A sausage roll is a British snack of sausage meat baked in pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: A sausage roll is minced meat in pastry, so the clue asks what kind of roll.

clue.text: Say, Nero's capital captivating traveller heading West

indicators.note: in an across answer heading west means read right to left
captivating means holding captive, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: Rome was the capital where Nero ruled
a rep is a commercial traveller

explanation.surface: Nero's capital city held a travelling salesman going west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captivating' gives ROREPME and 'heading West' turns it right to left. 'Nero's' reads as 'Nero is': he is an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nero ruled Rome as its fifth sovereign, so he is an example of an imperial ruler.

clue.text: On the back foot, to a degree

parts.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A team on the back foot, to some extent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the back foot' looks like a phrase meaning defensive, but 'On the back' is the definition and 'foot' gives FT.
explanation.definitionFit: Abaft is a nautical word for behind or towards the stern of a ship.

clue.text: Take one's vital fill, going to hibernate, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the word may be shown in another arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: An animal takes a deep breath before settling down to hibernate.
explanation.definitionFit: To inbreathe is to inhale, drawing in the air that keeps one alive.

clue.text: Rich person in Liberia shot magnificent beast

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other
shot means wrecked or broken, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the lion is the noble king of beasts

explanation.surface: A wealthy man in Liberia gunned down a splendid animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' looks like gunfire but signals an anagram, giving BILAIRE; 'in' places the beast inside that anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone worth a thousand million is extremely wealthy.

clue.text: On stage, suffer a block?

definitions.meaning: a performer who flops in front of an audience is said to perish
a stamping or cutting block used in metalwork, or a cube for gaming

explanation.surface: An actor on stage suffers a mental block.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses of one word: actors are said to do this when a show goes badly, and it is also a block for stamping metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedian flopping is said to perish on stage; a stamping tool or gaming cube is a block.

clue.text: Coach from London once closest to house

parts.note: travel away from London is traditionally 'down' (up to London, down from it)
a stage is a stagecoach, the old horse-drawn coach, hence 'once'

explanation.surface: An old-time coach left London heading for a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' is the theatre audience: downstage is the front of the stage, nearest the seats.
explanation.definitionFit: The front part of a stage lies nearest the audience, which theatre people call the house.

clue.text: Result of minor redesign of coins?

definitions.text: Result of minor redesign of coins?

parts.words: Result of minor redesign of coins?
parts.note: read literally, a slight alteration; and a pocketful of low-value coins is the everyday phrase

explanation.surface: What happens when the coinage is slightly redesigned.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a minor alteration, the phrase describes a small redesign; read as money, it means loose coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose coins of low value are known by this phrase, which can also mean a slight alteration.

clue.text: One in America going topless is rather dubious

indicators.note: going topless means losing the first letter
in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: the States is a familiar name for America
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Someone in America going without a top is somewhat questionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' gives THESITATES; 'going topless' then drops its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who wavers is uncertain, rather doubtful about acting.

clue.text: Quids in, promise to run in sporting championship

indicators.note: in means the pound sign goes inside the other piece

parts.note: to give your word is to promise
quid is slang for a pound, abbreviated L (librae)
a series is a run of events

explanation.surface: Money comes in when a promise is made to compete in a sporting championship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quids in' looks like the British phrase for being in profit, but splits into L (pounds) placed in WORD.
explanation.definitionFit: Baseball's annual championship in the USA goes by this name.

clue.text: Walker who's not heading for the point

definitions.meaning: a hiker who strolls in the country

definitions.text: who's not heading for the point
definitions.meaning: someone who talks on and on without getting to the point

explanation.surface: A hiker who keeps missing the headland.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses of one word: a hiker, and a person who talks at length without getting to the point.
explanation.definitionFit: A rambler hikes for pleasure, and one who rambles talks discursively without coming to the point.

clue.text: Mount Jesus was on in Jerusalem

definitions.meaning: a mount is an animal to ride
Jesus entered Jerusalem riding a donkey, as the gospels tell

explanation.surface: A mountain Jesus stood on in Jerusalem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' suggests a mountain such as the Mount of Olives, but it is an animal ridden: the donkey on which Jesus entered Jerusalem.
explanation.definitionFit: A donkey is a beast one rides, and Jesus rode one into Jerusalem on Palm Sunday.

clue.text: It might be largely an 'overreaction

indicators.note: might be suggests the word could become another arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Something could be mostly a matter of overreacting.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypersensitivity is the body's excessive immune response to a harmless substance.

clue.text: Natural son trouble-maker owned

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous troublemaker
to own up is to admit, or let on

explanation.surface: A naturally born son owned up to being a troublemaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Natural' is an old noun for a person of low intelligence, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural, in old usage, was a person born with little intelligence: a fool.

clue.text: Organ offered free — missing two notes at the top

indicators.note: missing means the named letters are taken away

parts.note: to deliver is to set free
D and E are musical notes

explanation.surface: An organ is offered free, though two notes at the top are missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' sounds musical, matching 'notes', but it is the body organ. The notes go from the top of DELIVER.
explanation.definitionFit: The liver is a large internal body part, an organ.

clue.text: A line put in rejected group accounts

indicators.note: put in means placed inside the other piece
rejected means thrown back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a set is a group

explanation.surface: An extra line goes into a rejected group's financial accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns SET into TES, and 'put in' places A and L inside. 'accounts' looks financial but means stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Stories or narratives are accounts of events.

clue.text: Male found in any battle

indicators.note: found in means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: some means any, as in 'have you some?'

explanation.surface: A man is found in some battle or other.
explanation.walkthrough: The Somme was a long First World War battle in northern France (1916).
explanation.definitionFit: The 1916 Western Front offensive is named after the French river, an example of a battle.

clue.text: Obsessed with boy sweetheart

parts.note: Al is a boy's name
a lover is a sweetheart

explanation.surface: Smitten with a boyfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: To be all over someone is to be extremely attentive or fixated on them, an idiom.

clue.text: One traditionally in black, now Ridge, even in green with frequency

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held: 'One traditionally in black, now Ridge, even in green with frequency' — 'now Ridge' is OCR garble with no scan; wordplay R E (even letters of green) + F fits but the clue text is unrecoverable
annotationWithheld.clue: One traditionally in black, now Ridge, even in green with frequency

clue.text: I may take new name, one held to be provisional

indicators.note: held means kept inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a term is a name or word for something
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: I might take on a new name, one held only temporarily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held' puts I (one) inside TERM, giving TERIM, after I and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Something interim lasts only until a permanent arrangement is made, so it is temporary.

clue.text: Flynn finally changing sides is a mistake

indicators.note: the last letter, L for left, is swapped for its opposite side, R for right

parts.note: Errol Flynn was the swashbuckling Hollywood actor

explanation.surface: The actor Flynn finally switching allegiances was an error of judgement.
explanation.walkthrough: L (left) and R (right) are the two sides; ERROL's final L becomes R.
explanation.definitionFit: A blunder or slip is a mistake.

clue.text: Technique not at a charge, usually at a crawl

parts.note: free means costing nothing
style is a manner or technique

explanation.surface: A technique that costs nothing and is usually done slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crawl' suggests going slowly, but it is the swimming stroke: in freestyle races swimmers almost always choose front crawl.
explanation.definitionFit: In swimming races where any stroke is allowed, competitors nearly always swim front crawl.
